Significant-bias threshold: Study's own criteria: desirable standard of analytical performance = coefficient of variation ≤6% (Fraser); a clinically important discordant result = one suggesting a 25-µg change in the recommended dosage (≥20%)
Clinical significance vs user APS: not reported in the information source
Sample type: Serum pool from patients receiving digoxin plus oral spironolactone (native co-medication)
Study method details: Pools built from 29 additional patients on digoxin plus an aldosterone antagonist because insufficient sample was available per patient; digoxin quantified in duplicate by all four immunoassays before and after ultrafiltration (Centrifree Micropartition System, 30 kDa, 2000 g for 20 min at room temperature)
Additional sources of bias: No gold-standard (LC-MS/MS) comparator - "The main limitation of this study is the lack of a gold-standard assay with which the results can be compared"; pooled rather than individual patient samples for the recovery work; digoxin spiked from a commercial ampoule; endogenous DLIF not excluded, and the PDF states the pool discrepancies "cannot only be explained in terms of analytical interferences due to aldosterone antagonists"; pooling across patients masks individual bias; only duplicate measurements; ultrafiltrate (free digoxin) values are printed in the same table but are a different measurand and are not tabulated here
Notes: The APS verdict is the missing literal because no reference method is designated for these native pools; note however that the printed inter-assay coefficient of variation of 18.6% is itself far above both the study's own desirable CV of 6% and the user APS of 3%.
